outcome: serum uric acid and calcium levels
cohort: 220 antenatal women ≥34 weeks of gestation (110 with hypertensive disorder of pregnancy and 110 normotensive controls)
finding: Hypertensive pregnant women had higher uric acid, lower calcium, and worse maternal and perinatal outcomes compared to normotensive pregnant women.
mod_finding: Induced labor followed by lower segment cesarean section was the most common mode of delivery in hypertensive cases, whereas, in controls, the majority had spontaneous onset of labor and delivered vaginally.
birth_weight: Mean neonatal birth weight in controls was 2.81 ± 0.295 Kg and in cases 2.56 ± 0.421 Kg
